subject.title: `doctor --fix` silently drops the `plugins.allow` entry for a bundled→externalized plugin (codex), unregistering the agent harness — and the gateway still reports healthy

question: Should a configured agent harness that fails to register make Gateway `/readyz` and status degraded, or should readiness remain limited to Gateway startup infrastructure with doctor/update as the sole enforcement point?
rationale: Both policies are technically viable, but they define a public operational contract for orchestrators and users; source inspection cannot determine the intended readiness boundary.

options.title: Degrade readiness
options.body: Keep `/healthz` as liveness, but make `/readyz` and status degraded with actionable plugin-install guidance whenever a configured harness owner is unavailable.

options.title: Keep readiness narrow
options.body: Leave Gateway readiness unchanged and instead make update/doctor fail loudly or block completion until every explicitly configured harness owner is installed and enabled.

recommendation.title: Degrade readiness
recommendation.body: Keep `/healthz` as liveness, but make `/readyz` and status degraded with actionable plugin-install guidance whenever a configured harness owner is unavailable.

likelyOwner.reason: This person merged and refined the existing configured-runtime diagnostics and has recent involvement in Gateway status semantics.
